title: Opportunistic kernel sampler with SLO-aware preference for mixed prefill/decode workloads
creator: Sophia Martinez
description:
Background: Our serving runtime currently selects kernels based on a static prioritized list combined with a lightweight cost lookup. This works well for homogeneous workloads but struggles with mixed prefill/decode traffic, heterogeneous GPU node types, and variable sequence-length distributions. We've seen 98th percentile latency regressions when bursts of long-prefill requests arrive on constrained nodes and when kernel warmstarts are poor.

Goal: Implement an opportunistic kernel sampler that (a) uses short micro-probes to gather latency/cost signals per-GPU and per-prefill/decode phase, (b) biases sampling towards kernels that historically meet SLOs while continuing low-rate exploration for potential better-cost alternatives, and (c) integrates sequence-length / architecture fingerprints into the sampling policy so decisions are context-aware. The sampler should be safe (no SLO violations during rollout), incrementally deployable, and instrumented for offline analysis and automatic rollback.
acceptance_criteria: Sampler runs as a hot-path module in runtime and returns a kernel choice within existing scheduling budget (<= 300us added decision latency)
99th percentile decode latency improves or remains within +/-2% for mixed traffic experiments compared to baseline on two test clusters
Sampler reduces average cost-per-token by >=3% for at least one customer workload in A/B experiment without SLO regressions
Comprehensive telemetry (per-choice latency histogram, seqlen-bucketed success rate, exploration rate) is emitted to console metrics
Feature flags allow canary rollout and immediate global disable; automated rollback policy is implemented
proposal:
Design: 1) Maintain a lightweight local registry per GPU (fingerprint -> kernel stats) where fingerprint = {arch_tag, seqlen_bucket, phase(prefill|decode)}. 2) On request arrival, consult registry: if high-confidence kernel exists that historically satisfied latency SLO for fingerprint, pick it. 3) Otherwise run opportunistic micro-probe: route a single sample request (or a scaled-down synthetic micro-benchmark) to try alternative kernel(s) with exponential backoff for safety. 4) Use an exploration schedule (epsilon-decay + decoupled optimism term) to continue low-rate trials of lower-cost kernels. 5) Maintain an online cost/latency estimator with windowed percentiles and decay to adapt to drift.

Implementation notes: keep probe overhead adjustable per-customer tier. For Dedicated customers with strict SLOs, default exploration epsilon=0.01. For free-tier hosted flows we can be slightly more aggressive. Probes must not leak across tenants; use strict isolation and tenant-scoped registries.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Probing adds extra system complexity and potential for SLO regressions if mis-configured — mitigated by conservative defaults and automated rollback
Per-GPU registries increase memory footprint but are bounded because fingerprints are bucketed (we limit to top-512 hot fingerprints)
Sampling noise can mislead cost estimator under bursty traffic; use EWMA + percentile smoothing and minimum observation counts before promoting a kernel
Additional telemetry increases observability costs — we will add sampling rate controls to metrics emission
implementation_plan: Phase 0: Spike - build local registry prototype + micro-probe harness and unit tests (2 wks)
Phase 1: Integrate with existing kernel chooser API and add fingerprinting logic (3 wks)
Phase 2: Add exploration schedule, safety checks, and telemetry hooks (2 wks)
Phase 3: Canary rollout to two test clusters with mixed prefills (1 wk)
Phase 4: A/B experiment against baseline on staged customer traffic, validate metrics and tweak epsilon (2 wks)
Phase 5: Rollout to Dedicated and Hosted with per-tier defaults and docs (2 wks)
test_plan: Unit tests for registry insert/evict and fingerprint bucketing
Microbench harness to simulate mixed prefill/decode work patterns and validate probe safety
Integration tests that run on dev cluster with heterogenous GPU types (A100, H100, older T4-like) emulated
Canary A/B run with synthetic traffic variations (seqlen 8/64/512) and real-customer-sampled replay
Chaos test: throttle a kernel's runtime to ensure fallback and rollback logic triggers correctly
notes: Keep default exploration aggressiveness conservative for infra-critical traffic. We plan to expose a per-route override for power users after initial rollout.
